description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the everyday-Perl battery (#1994): `use IO::Socket;` dies "Undefined subroutine &IO::Socket::UNIX::AF_UNIX called", and HTTP::Tiny falls with it.  The s491 write-up guessed "the Socket shim lacks a constant" -- REFUTED: lib/Socket.pm default-exports AF_UNIX (probe sock1.pl identical to perl).  PRE-EXISTING on main 268d7e00.

THE SHAPE: IO::Socket.pm does `require IO::Socket::UNIX` at run time; IO::Socket::UNIX.pm does `use IO::Socket;` -- IO::Socket is mid-load, its `sub import { ... Exporter::export 'Socket', $callpkg, @_ }` is already DEFINED (perl defines a file's named subs at compile time; PCL's emission also puts `(p-sub pl-import ...)` ABOVE `(p-require ...)`, checked), and perl calls it, which is how AF_UNIX reaches IO::Socket::UNIX.

MINIMAL REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/circ/{CircA.pm,CircB.pm,main.pl}):
  CircA.pm:  package CircA; require CircB; sub import { my $c = caller; no strict 'refs'; *{"${c}::hello"} = sub { "hello from CircA" } } 1;
  CircB.pm:  package CircB; use CircA; sub greet { hello() } 1;
  main.pl:   use lib '.'; use CircA; print CircB::greet(), "\n"; print hello(), "\n";
  perl: two lines "hello from CircA"        PCL: Undefined subroutine &CircB::hello called

THE MECHANISM (read, not guessed): cl/pcl-runtime.lisp `p-use`:
    (when (member rel-path *p-loading-modules* :test #'string=)
      (warn "Circular dependency detected: ~A" rel-path)
      (return-from p-use t))
The "Already loaded?" branch just above it DOES import (`(when do-import (%p-do-import ...))`); the circular branch must do the same, and perl prints no warning for a circular use, so the `warn` goes too (check nothing in Pl/t or the sweep asserts that text -- stale-guard rule s416).  perl's `import` on a half-loaded module finds whatever is defined SO FAR: a default Exporter `import` with `@EXPORT` not yet assigned (its `our @EXPORT = ...` is a run-time statement below the `require`) imports nothing, silently -- PCL must agree, and `%p-do-import` must not DIE on a module whose import method or @EXPORT is not there yet.  Probe all four quadrants vs perl: {custom import, Exporter import} x {the circular `use` happens from a run-time `require`, from a compile-time `use`}; plus `use Mod qw(name)` naming a symbol not yet exportable (perl: Exporter dies "is not exported" -- whatever perl does, match it), plus `require` (no import) stays a no-op.

THEN THE REAL TARGETS, by rows not by "it loads": `use IO::Socket; use IO::Socket::INET;` a loopback TCP echo between a forked child and the parent (perl's t/io/socket.t has the shape); `use HTTP::Tiny; HTTP::Tiny->new->get("http://127.0.0.1:PORT/")` against that loopback server (no external network in a guard).  `Exporter::export 'Socket', $callpkg, @_` (the function form) must work -- probe it alone first.  What is STILL missing after the circular fix is FILED per cause with the module's line, not patched by name (9a).

BAR: `cl/` change => full sweep + companion io/ + lib/ legs that load IO::Socket (`grep -a -l 'IO::Socket\|use Socket'`), CPAN board by ROWS (a module that used to fail at a circular use may now run further -- a row that ARRIVES is not a new failure), guard rows in Pl/t (the CircA/CircB fixture under a temp dir -- the mechanism, never a module name) INVERSE-verified, plus `modules.pl` from ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/central/ re-run: 57 of 73 before -> the new count.


=== DONE (s492a) ===
SHIPPED 8f106968.  perl's `use` is `require` + `import`, and `require` is
skipped when the file is in %INC -- which perl sets BEFORE it runs the file's
body.  So a module reached again while it is still loading takes the ordinary
already-loaded path: no second load, and `import` called on whatever the
half-loaded module has defined so far.  p-use returned early instead, importing
nothing, and warned on stderr about a state perl treats as ordinary (the warn
is gone; nothing in Pl/t, perl-tests or docs asserted its text -- grepped).

That one branch is why `use IO::Socket;` died "Undefined subroutine
&IO::Socket::UNIX::AF_UNIX called" and took IO::Socket::INET and HTTP::Tiny
with it.

FOUR QUADRANTS probed vs perl 5.40.3 -- {custom import, Exporter} x {partner
reached by require, by use} -- all identical after (scratch/s492a/circ/quad.pl):
a custom `sub import` is defined at compile time and DOES import; an Exporter
import whose `our @EXPORT = ...` sits BELOW the require imports NOTHING,
silently; a circular `require` imports nothing at all; the import LIST arrives.

MEASURED, not "it loads": the everyday battery's 73 core modules go 57 -> 59
(movers IO::Socket and HTTP::Tiny; IO::Socket::INET and IO::Socket::UNIX also
load but are not on the 73-module list), and a loopback TCP echo between a
forked child and the parent through IO::Socket::INET answers `echo:ping`,
identical to perl (scratch/s492a/m4-loopback.tree.out,
probes/m4-modules.{base,tree}.out).

What the modules STILL miss is filed per cause, never patched by name (9a):
#2011 (HTTP::Tiny stops at `$fh->blocking(0)`; lib/IO.pm croaks, needs an fcntl
primitive), #2010 (IPC::Cmd needs IO::Seekable::getpos/setpos), #2012
(File::Temp `tempdir(CLEANUP => 1)` with no template dies -- PRE-EXISTING,
probed on the base too).

Guard Pl/t/circular-use-01.t (4 rows, fixture modules written by the test so
the fact under test is the mechanism and never a module name; rows 1 and 4 FAIL
on a 268d7e00 extraction, 2 and 3 -- the inverse guards -- pass).
subject: EVERYDAY (IO::Socket, IO::Socket::INET, HTTP::Tiny -- everything networking): a CIRCULAR `use` of a module that is MID-LOAD skips its IMPORT -- perl skips only the LOAD (%INC is already set) and still calls `import`; mechanism LOCATED: `p-use`'s "Circular dependency?" branch warns and returns before `%p-do-import`
